title: Thomas More Refuses the Oath
text:
Thomas More was a lawyer, scholar and author of Utopia, and from 1529 he was Lord Chancellor of England, the highest office under the king. When Henry VIII broke with the pope to end his marriage to Catherine of Aragon and marry Anne Boleyn, More could not agree. In 1532 he resigned and retired into private life.

In 1534 Parliament passed the Act of Succession, and all leading subjects were required to swear an oath that accepted Anne's children as heirs and rejected the authority of the pope. More was willing to accept the succession itself, which he said Parliament could settle, but he would not swear the oath as written. He refused to explain his reasons in detail, so as not to give the king grounds to charge him. He was sent to the Tower of London in April 1534.

After more than a year in prison he was tried for treason on July 1, 1535, convicted largely on the testimony of Richard Rich, which More said was false. He was beheaded on July 6. A contemporary report says he told the crowd he died the king's good servant, but God's first.
lesson: Integrity sometimes means refusing to say what you do not believe, even when saying it would be easy and refusing costs everything.
people: Thomas More, Henry VIII, Richard Rich
source: Records of More's trial; William Roper, The Life of Sir Thomas More; the Paris News Letter account of his execution
